subject.title: sessions.patch has no plugin-ownership check, unlike its sessions.delete sibling

question: Should this public cross-plugin `sessions.patch` ownership bypass be fixed through the normal public bugfix path, or routed through security-owned advisory/backport handling first?
rationale: The source evidence supports a narrow fix, but the affected behavior is a stable gateway plugin-isolation boundary, so automation should not choose the disclosure and release-handling path on its own.

options.title: Approve narrow public fix
options.body: Patch `sessions.patch` to reuse the existing plugin-runtime ownership invariant and add focused regression tests, while maintainers decide release-note or backport wording.

options.title: Route through security handling
options.body: Pause public repair automation and handle advisory, disclosure, and backport decisions through the repository security process.

options.title: Declare current asymmetry intentional
options.body: Keep the current behavior only if maintainers explicitly want plugin-runtime callers with admin scope to patch foreign sessions and can document why delete remains stricter.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow public fix
recommendation.body: Patch `sessions.patch` to reuse the existing plugin-runtime ownership invariant and add focused regression tests, while maintainers decide release-note or backport wording.

likelyOwner.reason: Tyler is the strongest feature-history routing signal for the gateway session lifecycle/API surface that owns this boundary.
